content:
mike: Follow-up from today's all-hands Q&A on pricing/usage  can someone summarize the canonical "credits vs quotas" language for the handbook? want one clear paragraph we can point to.
sophia: Short canonical blurb: Credits are prepaid consumption units used on Hosted plans; quotas are enforced limits (requests/min, tokens/day) applied per org/route/pool. Dedicated customers buy reserved capacity instead of credits and have configurable throughput + burst windows.
mike: Perfect. Couple of specifics that came up: 1) Do trial credits roll over? 2) Can Hosted burst above quota temporarily? 3) How do we handle priority when infra constrained?
shenry: Answers: 1) Trial credits expire at end of trial window (no automatic rollover). 2) Hosted supports short bursts up to a tiered ceiling (example: dev tier = 50k tokens/5min, growth = 200k tokens/5min) if there's cluster headroom; otherwise we gracefully throttle or route to fallback model. 3) Priority: Dedicated pools are isolated and get allocation guarantees; Hosted traffic is scheduled by org priority and region headroom. In severe constraints we shift Hosted to lower-cost compatible variants or queue requests; we avoid killing in-flight requests.
mike: Are there programmatic endpoints customers can call to show remaining credits/quota in their app?
elaine: Yep, planned public endpoint: GET /v1/orgs/{org_id}/usage (ETA: next week). It will return remaining credit balance, current rate limit windows, per-route quotas, and recent usage metrics.
We include examples and an SDK helper to fetch a short summary.
sophia: Billing nuance: prepaid hosted credits are non-refundable under standard self-serve terms. Enterprise agreements can include rollover or refund clauses negotiated in contract.
ops-bot: infra-note: quota-monitoring agent now alerts at 80% and 95% thresholds for org-level token usage.
billing-bot: reminder: prepaid credits are consumed before invoiced usage; apply credits via customer billing portal.
mike: Can Support & Sales get a one-pager with bullet defaults (trial tokens, default rate limits, burst ceilings) + the API link?
sophia: I'll draft the one-pager and post in #docs when ready. Henry  can you verify the tiered burst numbers?
shenry: Will validate numbers and reply here by EOD.
mike: Thanks all :thumbsup:
